lead: A reference project on the language of sulfur chemistry: German and English terms, the compounds they name, and the evidence behind each statement.

sections.heading: Start with a governed reference
paragraphs: The first reference record built under the current rules covers molybdenum disulfide (MoS2): its formula, its layered bulk structure, the 1T, 2H and 3R polytypes, and two independent determinations of the 2H lattice parameter. It rests on {{GOV:mos2_admitted_evidence}} admitted evidence records, each traced to the study or database that produced it.

sections.heading: The question in our name
paragraphs: 'Bisulfid' and 'bisulfide' differ by one letter. Whether 'Bisulfid' is simply the German spelling of the English term is itself a terminology claim, and it is handled like any other claim on this site: it will be stated as fact only after its sources are verified and admitted. {{GOV:bisulfid_claims_pending}} related terminology claims are registered and still under review.

links.label: Bisulfid and bisulfide: the terminology record

sections.heading: How a statement reaches a reference page
paragraphs: A source is first identified and checked, then qualified for a specific use. A passage from it is recorded as evidence with its exact location, and a claim is approved only against admitted evidence. Numbers are quoted as their sources print them; when two determinations differ, both are shown rather than averaged. A page is published only if it adds knowledge that no other page on the site already holds.

sections.heading: English and German
paragraphs: The site is maintained in English and German. A German page exists when it answers a German-language question, such as which form a German technical text uses, rather than as a copy of an English page.

sections.heading: What you will not find here
paragraphs: BISULFID does not give safety, handling, medical, procurement or investment guidance. For those, use the safety data sheet of the specific product and a qualified professional.
